football_evidence.assessment: Some measured evidence supports EdgeDesk’s lean toward Auburn, and its own breakdown accounts for about 1.2 of the 2.1 points, but not the full gap. It is a research question, not a bet.

contradicting: When Auburn has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Auburn’s offense has allowed a sack on 10.7% of its dropbacks, and LSU’s defense sacks the quarterback on 11.4% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.6%).
When Auburn has the ball (the passing game against the pass defense): Auburn’s offense averages 6.3 yards per pass attempt, and LSU’s defense allows 5.9 yards per pass attempt (FBS average 7.4).

When Auburn has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): Auburn’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 12.1% of its runs, and LSU’s defense stops 26.8% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.4%).

When LSU has the ball (early downs): LSU’s offense succeeds on 52.0% of its first- and second-down plays, and Auburn’s defense allows success on 46.0% of first- and second-down plays (FBS average 42.7%).
